title: Todos of Rome
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Berakhot 19a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.19a.12): “Rav Yosef taught: Todos of Rome accustomed the people of Rome to eat kids roasted whole in the paschal style on the nights of Passover (abroad). Shimon ben Shetach sent to him: Were you not Todos, I would decree a ban upon you.” The warning is also quoted at [Pesachim 53a:14](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.53a.14), where the senders are unnamed.[^2] They asked there whether Todos was a great man or a violent man, and they said: “Come and hear: This too Todos of Rome expounded: What did Chananyah, Mishael and Azaryah see that they gave themselves up for the sanctification of the Name?” etc. Rabbi Yose bar Avin said that he used to provide business capital for Torah scholars.[^1]
So it is in the [Jerusalem Talmud, Pesachim, beginning of chapter 7](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Pesachim.7.1.8): he used to assist the sages with their livelihood.

notes.text: The corresponding discussion is at [Pesachim 53b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.53b.6-9), beside Hyman’s 53a. It has the fiery-furnace homily and Rabbi Yose bar Avin’s account of Todos providing scholars with business capital. Berakhot names Shimon ben Shetach as the sender of the warning.

[Pesachim 53a:14](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.53a.14) introduces the account in Rabbi Yose’s name and says “they sent to him.” The warning begins there and continues onto 53b, where the Gemara later discusses Todos’s standing, his homily, and his support for Torah scholars.
